To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TTCN-3 language is well suited for the testing of embedded software in electronic devices.
TTCN-3 has a lot of potential to improve the product testing process in the electronic devices development.
TTCN-3 is a powerful tool for test development and test execution.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: - TTCN-3 as a formal specification language for test cases and test suites - TTCN-2 and TTCN-3 interoperability - TTCN- 3 test case and test suite implementation - Test automation - TTCN- and TTCN-2 to TTCN-3 conversion - TTCN-1 to TTCN-2 conversion - Test case and test suite management - TTCN- test case and test suites in a test management system - TTCN- testing and
the introduction of TTCN- 3 as an additional testing tool into the product development and test environment of an electronic devices manufacturer.

the following topics: - Definition of test suites for electronic devices, - Test execution in an automated test environment, - Integration of TTCN-2 and TTCN-3 test suites, - Integration of test suites into the product development environment, - Integration and use of TTCN-1 and TTCN-2 in the test environment, - Test automation in the product development process, - Test execution and test result evaluation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TTCN-3 can be introduced in the process of testing electronic devices and can be beneficial.
TTCN-3 is not a panacea for the problems in testing of electronic devices.
TTCN-3 has a high potential for improvement of test automation, but that this potential can not yet be exploited.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TTCN-3 has to be introduced into the development process in a way that is compatible with existing procedures and environments.
the TTCN-3 language and its associated tools and techniques are well suited for the development of test specifications and test implementations in the context of electronic devices manufacturing.
TTCN-3 has the potential to become a standard language for the definition of test cases and for their execution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TTCN-3 language is not yet ready for the product development process, but that it is a promising technology for the future.
TTCN-3 is a suitable language for test specification and execution in the context of electronic devices manufacturing and the introduction of the language into the process is feasible.
TTCN-3 has to be introduced in an evolutionary way, starting from simple test definitions, which are easy to implement in a testing environment.
